faq.are_responses_real_human: NO. Responses are automated machine submissions, NOT real humans. They are engineered to SIMULATE natural human patterns using shuffled text pools, proportional Likert extrapolation, anti-streak shuffling, and variable delays with ±4% jitter.
faq.does_system_use_ai_for_form_answers: NO. The AI (Groq) is ONLY for this copilot help chat. Form answers are generated mathematically (Largest Remainder Method) and submitted via direct HTTP POST requests.
faq.how_are_responses_created: FormPilot uses: 1) User-configured text pools (e.g. COT, COB) for text fields, 2) Proportional scaling of user sample rating counts (e.g. 5:2, 4:3, 3:1) using the Largest Remainder Method, and 3) Global shuffling across respondents.
faq.no_sample_provided: If no sample counts are provided, FormPilot distributes answers uniformly across available choices, or you can click 'Auto-Fill Positive Preset (4s & 5s)'.
faq.why_cant_it_read_google_form: The form is likely private, restricted to organization users only, or has 'Limit to 1 response' enabled (which forces Google login). Fix: Turn OFF 'Limit to 1 response' and organization restrictions in Form Settings, then copy link from Send -> Link.
faq.what_delay_means: The delay is the gap FormPilot waits between submitting each respondent to prevent IP rate limits and simulate real-time submission pacing.
faq.non_google_forms: NO. FormPilot is exclusively built for Google Forms (docs.google.com/forms and forms.gle). Other platforms like Typeform or Microsoft Forms are not supported.
faq.limitations: Only public Google Forms (no sign-in or organization restrictions), no CAPTCHA/file upload questions, Google Forms only, and server-side submission timestamp clock cannot be faked via HTTP POST (must edit Column A in the linked Google Sheet for past dates).
faq.is_open_source: YES. FormPilot is 100% open-source, running locally on your computer with Python and Flask.
faq.where_to_put_target_respondents: In Step 2 ('Configure & Scale'). After scanning in Step 1, click 'Configure Answers & Respondent Pool' (or click Step 2 in the top bar). The 'Target Respondents' box is right at the top.
faq.supports_essays_and_other_styles: YES. Supports Short Answer, Paragraph/Essay, Multiple Choice, Checkboxes, Linear Scale (1-5), and Multiple-Choice Grids. Text fields use user-defined text variation pools.

workflow_steps.step_1: Connect & Scan public Google Form URL (extracts questions, entry IDs, Likert grids).
workflow_steps.step_2: Configure target respondents, text variation pools, Likert rating sample counts, and custom delay intervals.
workflow_steps.step_3: Preview dataset table, re-shuffle order, or export plan JSON.
workflow_steps.step_4: Live execution with progress bar, countdown timer, Pause/Stop controls, and completion menu (Re-Run, Change Rating, Home).
